precepts.text: An example: Anna, a prophetess, of the tribe of Aser, a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.
precepts.point: The high priest told him that there was such money laid up for the relief of widows and fatherless children, and that some of it belonged to Hircanus son of Tobias, a man of great dignity, and not as that wicked Simon had misinformed: in all four hundred talents of silver and two hundred of gold. And that it was altogether impossible that such wrong should be done unto them that had committed it to the holiness of the place.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
Paul says a widow indeed “trusteth in God, and continueth in supplications and prayers night and day.” Luke gives an example of exactly that.

“And there was one Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser: she was of a great age, and had lived with an husband seven years from her virginity; And she was a widow of about fourscore and four years, which departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day.”

She did not depart from the temple. She served God with fastings and prayers, night and day. That is what widows did. She was married to one man, well over threescore years old, and she gave her life to prayer for Israel.

Those were the widows the temple money was laid up to relieve in Onias’s day: sisters who had dedicated themselves to the Lord. To betray that money to the Greeks was to take the bread from women like Anna.

precepts.text: She brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes: the same handling our forefathers gave the lambs brought to Jerusalem. Thus fulfilling prophecy; Christ is our passover.
precepts.point: First the weekly Sabbath, whose true meaning we just read: rest going into the kingdom. Then the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord's passover, which we just finished celebrating, and the fifteenth day begins the feast of unleavened bread: seven days ye must eat unleavened bread. The unleavened bread is Christ's sinless life, and the haste out of Egypt besides.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:) To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child.”

To be taxed together you have to be married, brothers. You have to have papers, jointly. Not a toilet paper: years ago a brother wrote an instrument of divorce on toilet paper, because he did not really value her or count her as his wife.

“And so it was, that, while they were there, the days were accomplished that she should be delivered. And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes”. They wrapped Christ in swaddling clothes, the same thing our forefathers did with the lambs when they brought them to Jerusalem.

Born in Bethlehem where the passover lambs were raised, wrapped the way they were wrapped, offered in Jerusalem at passover. Thus fulfilling prophecy. So we know Christ was our passover.

precepts.text: When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, and the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem with a pair of turtledoves: circumcision plus sacrifice, the manner of Moses.
precepts.point: Luke 2 confirms it: eight days accomplished for the circumcising of the child, the days of her purification according to the law of Moses, presented to the Lord with a sacrifice of two turtledoves.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
In Acts 15 certain men came down from Judea and taught, “Except ye be circumcised after the manner of Moses, ye cannot be saved.” Why does it say after the manner of Moses and not just circumcision? Leviticus 12 shows the manner of Moses. A woman who “conceived seed, and born a man child” is unclean seven days; “in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised”; she continues in the blood of her purifying thirty-three more days, forty in all for a boy and eighty for a girl. When the days are fulfilled she brings a lamb and a pigeon or turtledove for a burnt offering and a sin offering, and if she cannot afford a lamb, “two turtles, or two young pigeons”. The priest makes the atonement, and the offering covers the child as well as the mother.

Luke 2 confirms it with Mary and Christ. Mary conceived seed and bore a man child. “And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” That is the eighth day of Leviticus 12.

“And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord”, because “Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord”. Then comes the offering: “to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.” Those are the offerings Leviticus 12:8 names.

So behind circumcision after the manner of Moses comes sacrifice. It is circumcision with the eighth day, the days of purifying and the offering for the woman and the child all tied together. That is what the men from Judea were pressing on the Gentiles, and that is why the scripture calls it the manner of Moses.

precepts.text: Three times a year all males appear before the Lord: unleavened bread, weeks and tabernacles.
precepts.point: Christ went up at twelve for Passover. He was born at Passover and died at Passover.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Luke says Mary “laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.” The inn is a hotel. Why was there no room in the hotels? Deuteronomy 16:16 shows it: “Three times in a year shall all thy males appear before the Lord thy God in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles”.

The feast of unleavened bread is the Passover; the feast of weeks is Pentecost. Three times a year all Israel had to go up to Jerusalem, and at that time every inn was full because everybody came up for the feast. There was no room in the inn because it was the Passover.

Christ was not born in the manger. The prophecy in Song of Solomon 8:5 says, “I raised thee up under the apple tree: there thy mother brought thee forth”. Mary brought him forth under the apple tree, and after that took him to the manger, because the city was full for the feast.

precepts.text: Shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
precepts.point: Christ went up at twelve for Passover. He was born at Passover and died at Passover.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.” The shepherds were out in the field with the flock at night. That does not happen in the winter.

A manger is a feeding trough in the barn. In the wintertime the animals are brought into the barn to stay warm; nobody is abiding in the field then. Around tabernacles, the ingathering, is when they bring in all their animals and all the crops to prepare for the mean season. So shepherds in the field by night fits the springtime, and Christ was born in the springtime, at the Passover.

Christmas has nothing to do with Christ. Do not give heed to Jewish fables, which turn you away from the truth; that is what Christmas does, it turns you away from the truth and from serving God.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem”. East of Jerusalem is Babylon and the lands of the different captivities. Those wise men were Israel, living in the lands east of Jerusalem, “Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Jews? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.”

The star they saw was a chariot, a light, what they call UFOs today, not a celestial body in the night sky. A planet cannot do what this did: “the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, till it came and stood over where the young child was.” It guided them on the earth and stood over the house.

“And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother”. The house, not the manger. Christians show the wise men in a barn giving gifts to a baby, but time had passed; Christ was a young child now, a toddler of around two, walking and forming words. The wise men had been following that star at least two years. They were not three men; three is the number of the gifts, “gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.” They came as a caravan. With those gifts Christ was taken care of; he was not poor.

Herod, an Edomite who converted to being a Jew, a white man set up as king of Judea by Rome, “slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.” Thousands of black babies. That shows the child was around two when the wise men came. And when you see the synagogues of Satan killing babies in Palestine today, it does not surprise us; that is in their nature.

precepts.why:
“Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover.” “And when he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem after the custom of the feast.” When did Christ turn twelve? At the Passover. Christ was born on the Passover and he died on the Passover.

1 Corinthians 5:7: “For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. Christ is our Passover. That is why the inn was full when he was born: all Israel was up in Jerusalem for the feast.

December 25th goes back to the 25th of Kislev, when Antiochus IV Epiphanes desecrated the temple, set up Zeus and swine's flesh, and forced our people to worship Greek gods. God has festival days and Satan does too: we have our dedication and Satan has Christmas; we have our Passover and Satan has Easter. Stop giving heed to Jewish fables and following St. Nicholas and the Pope; that lie turns you away from the truth.

precepts.text: When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus; Christ kept the same law.
precepts.point: That did not change. On the eighth day they came to circumcise John the Baptist, and when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
“And when eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called JESUS, which was so named of the angel before he was conceived in the womb.”

Christ himself kept the same law. He was circumcised when the eight days were accomplished, the eighth day of Leviticus 12:3, and he was named at that time with the name the angel gave before he was conceived.

John the Baptist on the eighth day, and Christ on the eighth day: the law of circumcision did not change, and it stands for us.

precepts.text: When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished; Mary kept the law of the forty days.
precepts.point: Mary is the fulfilment of that: when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord; Mary had to do this law.

note.label: Leviticus 12: The Law of Purification After Childbirth

precepts.why:
After a male child the mother is unclean forty days: seven days of separation plus “three and thirty days” of purifying. In all that time “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.”

Mary is the fulfilment of that: “when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord.” Mary had to do this law. She waited out the forty days, and only then came to the sanctuary with the child.

precepts.text: I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and that with cares. For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.
precepts.point: The swaddling clothes are the mark of an ordinary entrance into life. The wise man says plainly that there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.

note.label: Luke 2: The Birth at Bethlehem and the Child in the Temple

precepts.why:
The sign given to the shepherds is the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. The swaddling clothes are the mark of an ordinary entrance into life, and the wise man says it plainly: “I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth, And in my mother’s womb was fashioned to be flesh in the time of ten months”.

“And when I was born, I drew in the common air, and fell upon the earth, which is of like nature, and the first voice which I uttered was crying, as all others do. I was nursed in swaddling clothes, and that with cares. For there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.” Christ the Lord, born in the city of David, came in by the same beginning every king has.

precepts.text: God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law.
precepts.point: When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus. He was born under the law and everything done for him was done after the law.

note.label: Luke 2: The Birth at Bethlehem and the Child in the Temple

precepts.why:
Paul writes that “when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law, To redeem them that were under the law, that we might receive the adoption of sons.”

He was made under the law, and everything done for him was done after the law: the circumcising of the child when eight days were accomplished is the law being kept on him.
